builds.author: Claude
builds.title: Irelia — Lulu in the movement engine
builds.summary: An untested idea: the Vendetta RQ list that came second at Los Angeles, with four of its weakest-supported slots spent on two Radiance cards that feed the deck's real engine — moving and re-readying units.
builds.basis: Xeno, #2 overall, Riftbound Regional Qualifier — Los Angeles (Vendetta, 1,962 players on Day 1). The Radiance-era evidence for Irelia is thin and poor: 3 placed lists in the online previews, best #21 of 74, so this starts from her last proven list instead.

changes.what: −1 Abandon, −1 Pyke, Returned, −1 Twilight Shroud, −1 Not So Fast
changes.why: The four slots with least support: Abandon and Pyke are in about a third of placed Vendetta Irelia lists and none of the preview ones; Twilight Shroud and Not So Fast fell from 54% and 64% to 33%.

Radiance, untried with Irelia. "When I move, you may have another unit's base Might become 4 this turn." Irelia's legend readies a chosen unit, Tideturner, Ride the Wind and Flash move them; every move is a Lulu trigger, beside Stellacorn Herder's draw.
0% before Radiance, 2 of 3 preview Irelia lists. Reaction +2 Might; Show Off one of the list's 5 gear (Boots of Swiftness, Zhonya's Hourglass, Guardian Angel) and it readies up to 2 runes.

plan: Unchanged from the Vendetta list: develop Stellacorn Herder and Tideturner, then use the legend to ready a unit you choose so it can move again — each move draws with Herder.

Lulu turns the same moves into combat: a move sets another unit's base Might to 4 this turn, so a small unit becomes a real attacker, or a defender at a battlefield you are contesting. Whether 'another unit' is best yours or theirs is a judgement per board, and untested here.

matchups.note: Untested. Nothing in the data plays Lulu with Irelia yet; this is a reading of the cards, to be played and logged.

builds.sim: Goldfish, 8,000 games, against its base list: Energy spent turns 1–4 17.2 → 17.8 on the play (18.6 → 19.9 on the draw); units on board by turn 3 2.4 → 2.5; stuck on Power turn 3 0% → 0%; mulligan keep all; runes 6/6 fine. Curve and mana only — the engine itself is not simulated.

builds.author: Claude
builds.title: Kai'Sa Void — the Nova runner-up
builds.summary: Second of 74 at NovaRiftbound #5, an unsanctioned online preview event before Radiance was legal. Every one of the 12 placed Kai'Sa lists from the preview events is within 70% of the consensus: the most settled deck so far, in a format that has barely started.
builds.basis: YBE piorro - NovaRiftbound's $2,000 Online Showdown 5, #2 of 74, NovaRiftbound's $2,000 Online Showdown 5. 95% consensus overlap.

changes.why: Kept as played; the placed lists barely differ from each other.

plan: Kai'Sa's legend exhausts to add one Power of any domain, for spells only — the deck is a spell deck with large units behind it.

The units are the payoff: Thousand-Tailed Watcher gives enemy units -3 Might this turn (to a minimum of 1); Brynhir Thundersong stops opponents playing cards the turn it lands; The Empyrean, new in Radiance, can Show Off a card to Predict and draw 2. Bilgewater Tracker, also new, deals 1 to each of up to 2 units on arrival.
Temporal Breach is Hidden: it banishes a unit and replays it at the same location, ignoring its cost — a reset for your own play effects as much as an answer.

matchups.note: No Radiance-era matchup records yet.

builds.sim: Goldfish, 8,000 games: keep every opener; Energy spent turns 1–4 18.0 on the play / 20.3 on the draw; 3.0 units by turn 3; stuck on turn 3 0%; 7/5 runes fine.

builds.author: Claude
builds.title: Kennen Tempest — the Chaos majority build
builds.summary: The build most placed Kennen lists play (17 of 20 are within 70% of the consensus), from its best finish. The Haven winner is a different, Order-heavy deck — see its list below. Both Kennen events were unsanctioned online previews played before Radiance was legal.
builds.basis: terrencem - Haven Online Challenger Series #5 - October 11th 2026 (Radiance Preview), #5 of 50, Haven Online Challenger Series #5 - October 11th 2026 (Radiance Preview). 90% of its main deck matches the consensus. Chosen over the #1 list because that one (35% overlap, Illaoi and Seal of Unity, 8 Order runes) is one player's build; this one is what the field converged on and still finished top 8.

changes.why: Kept as played. Copy the #1 list from the lists below if you want the Order build instead.

plan: Kennen's legend empowers whenever you play a card from anywhere other than your hand, then disempowers to give a unit Assault 2. The deck is built to do that every turn.

Lightning Rush looks at 3 and trashes the rest, and has Flow — playable again from the trash. Trifarian Captain looks at 4 and draws a cheap unit or gear. Nocturne, Horrifying can be played for one Power when you see it from the top of your deck. Each of those is a card played from somewhere other than your hand.
The trash filling up is the second engine: Rhasa the Sunderer costs 1 less for each card in it. Seal of Discord adds Chaos to get there.
9 Chaos / 3 Order. The simulator suggests bottoming 5+ cost cards in the opener.

matchups.note: No matchup records yet. The two online preview events show Kennen beside Riven, Yasuo and Kai'Sa at the top; that is a field, not a matchup table.

builds.sim: Goldfish, 8,000 games: mulligan by bottoming 5+ cost cards; Energy spent turns 1–4 16.3 on the play / 17.4 on the draw; 3.4 units by turn 3; stuck on turn 3 1%; 9/3 runes fine.

builds.author: Claude
builds.title: Kha'Zix — Radiance rebuild: choose every fight
builds.summary: An untested rebuild on Jun's post-ban midrange list: seven slots go to Radiance cards that do the deck's one job better — make the enemy unit be alone where you want it, and make the fight there unanswerable. Jun's own lists stay as they are; this is a list to test against them, and to show him.
builds.basis: Jun's "Kha'Zix Midrange (post-ban)" — his list, from a player who lists Best-of-Kha'Zix wins at RQ Utrecht and Barcelona (his own record). His 33 core cards are kept: Faefolk, Void Assault, Mutating Horror, Rengar, Fizz, Kinkou Initiate, Punch First, Rampage, Star-Crossed, Sabotage, Up from the Deep, Switcheroo, Tail-Cloaked Matriarch, his runes, battlefields and sideboard.

changes.why: The weakest-supported card in the data: the 9 placed Kha'Zix lists with Vex finished on average 42 percentile points worse than the 6 without. Nine lists is noise-sized, so this is the change to undo first if the deck feels worse. Vex also stuns only units the opponent plays — reactive, where every other card here makes fights happen. Moved out entirely; Jun's sideboard is unchanged.

changes.what: −1 Grim Resolve, −1 Tornado Warrior, −1 Zed, Without a Sound, −2 Traveling Merchant
changes.why: The slots with the least to do in the isolation plan: a third pump behind Punch First and Rampage, a facedown 3-drop, a second movement payoff behind Shadow Order Disciple, and Merchant's discard-draw. Grim Resolve lists also finished worse in the data (17 points, 9 lists).

"[Reaction] Move an enemy unit that moved this turn." The isolation tool the deck never had at Reaction speed: when they move two units in to defend or attack, move one away and the other is alone for Mutating Horror. In 69 lists, none of them Kha'Zix.

"Opponents can't play spells this turn. Move a friendly unit to an occupied enemy battlefield." The turn your fight cannot be answered with a trick — and that includes their facedown spells, because flipping a hidden card is playing it (rules §811.1.c.3). Hidden units can still come in. The finisher into the Reaction-heavy Calm/Chaos field (Irelia, Riven, Vex).

2-drop with Disarm (when it attacks, an enemy unit there gets −1 Might this turn) and Ganking, replacing Traveling Merchant at the same cost. A cheap body that moves between battlefields to set up a lone defender.
"[E]: [Stun] an enemy unit." Every turn, on your Main Phase before the fight (an activated ability without Reaction, so only then — §381.1): the defender you isolate deals no combat damage.

"When I attack or defend, deal damage equal to my Might to all enemy units here. I don't deal combat damage." 4 to everything at his battlefield — into the go-wide decks (Rek'Sai, Viktor's Recruits, Spiderlings) that never present the lone unit Kha'Zix wants.

plan: Jun's plan is unchanged: develop first, spells second; win fights for XP; walk the exhausted winner home with the legend so the conquest is not punished.

What changes is control of the fight. Siren's Song and Faefolk/Void Assault decide who is alone; Pitiless Stalker stuns the defender before you go; Cataclysm makes one fight per game spell-proof; Graves cleans up when they refuse to be alone.
On the cost side, the goldfish says it is a touch slower — more of the 40 is held interaction and two threats cost 6 — so the early turns lean harder on Faefolk, Disciple and Siren of the Shallows.

matchups.note: Cataclysm is for them: one combat they cannot Defy, Discipline or Defiant Dance. Untested.
Graves is for them; Siren's Song still splits a pair. Untested.
Unchanged from Jun's plan — Sabotage for Time Warp; this list adds nothing for it.

builds.sim: Goldfish, 8,000 games, against Jun's midrange list: Energy spent turns 1–4 17.1 → 16.2 on the play (19.1 → 17.9 on the draw); units by turn 3 3.5 → 3.5; Might on board turn 4 15.3 → 14.1; stuck on Power turn 3 4% → 6%; mulligan keep all; runes 6/6 fine. Slower by about one Energy over four turns, the price of the extra interaction. The engine is not simulated.

builds.author: Claude
builds.title: Mordekaiser — Amplifier aristocrats (risky Radiance)
builds.summary: The sacrifice engine pushed all the way into Radiance: every outlet does something when it kills (Shimmering Swimmer deals 2, Deathgrip pumps and draws, Detonation Amplifier draws and doubles Deathknells where it stands), and the fodder hits back when it dies (Mournful Spirit kills a unit or gear, Hunting Dog leaves a Bird). Built ahead of the crowd, not against it: every Radiance card here is rising in posted Mordekaiser lists this week. 16 copies in and 16 out from the anchored list — past the 6–9 winners usually stray, right at the 16 past which it is a different deck (docs/deckbuilding.md) — and nothing backs it yet, so it is marked untested.
builds.basis: Starts from builds/mordekaiser-sacrifice.json (the consensus of the 5 placed preview lists) and changes it toward the week's movement in the 34 posted Mordekaiser lists (data/rising.json, 2026-10-13–2026-10-19 against 2026-09-29–2026-10-12). No result backs this list.

changes.why: Rising 3% → 21%. Deploy at a battlefield: kill another friendly unit or gear to draw 1, and friendly Deathknells there trigger an additional time — Dredger's Bird twice, Mournful Spirit's kill twice. The card you won with at the Pre-Rift. Lost if they take that battlefield.

The riskiest pick: 6% → 9%. An outlet that is also removal — kill a friendly unit or gear as you play it, deal 2 to a unit. Kill a Dredger, get the Bird, deal 2, and put a card in the trash for the legend.

Rising 0% → 12% and 3% → 15%. Fodder that pays: the Spirit kills a unit or gear at its battlefield when it dies; the Dog leaves a Deflect Bird (a token: it is the next sacrifice, but never fuel — §186.1).
Rising 9% → 29%, 44% → 68%. More cards that die into tokens; Escaped Grayback stays at 3: the outlet that grows.
50% → 41% — the only Reaction outlet: sacrifice mid-fight to pump the survivor and draw.

changes.what: −3 Kai'Sa, Survivor, −1 Harnessed Dragon, −2 Vanguard Captain, −2 Spectral Matron, −1 Xin Zhao, Vigilant, −1 Vi, Peacekeeper, −1 Soaring Scout, −1 Seal of Unity, −2 Sacrifice, −1 Honest Broker, −1 Ferrous Forerunner
changes.why: The slots that do not feed the engine. Kai'Sa, Survivor (56% → 38%) and Sacrifice (41% → 26%) are falling in posted lists anyway; the 8-drop Dragon gives way to Mordekaiser, Dominating and the Spirits as the removal. The second Sacrifice and an Honest Broker (50% → 32%) made room for Hidden Blade (20 Oct).

Added 20 Oct, against the evidence bar: only 1 of the 5 Radiance-preview placings runs it, though 56% of all posted Mordekaiser lists do (falling 63% → 50%, data/rising.json). [Hidden] [Action], kill a unit at a battlefield, and its controller draws 2. Here that controller can be you: on your own unit it is a Reaction-speed outlet that triggers a Deathknell, puts a real card in the trash for the legend, and draws you 2 — Sacrifice without needing a Mighty unit. On theirs it is the clean answer to a big unit this deck lacked, at the price of two cards for them. It reaches only units at a battlefield, never your base.

plan: Same engine as the anchored list (builds/mordekaiser-sacrifice.json): the legend banishes cards from your trash for Power to play units and gear, and only real cards get there — tokens off the board cease to exist (§186.1). So sacrifice cards, keep the tokens as the next sacrifice.

The difference is that every sacrifice does something twice over. Swimmer kills to deal 2; Deathgrip kills to pump and draw; Amplifier kills to draw and then doubles every Deathknell at its battlefield; Grayback kills to grow; Hidden Blade kills to draw 2 (aim it at your own unit at a battlefield); Baited Hook kills to play a bigger unit from the top 5 for free (feed it Ferrous Forerunner for Twice Slain or Rift Herald). Mournful Spirit dying at an Amplifier kills two things.
Twice Slain (7 Energy, 1 Power, Accelerate, Assault 3) is the threat the trash pays for, and it survives by killing a friendly unit — one more outlet. Realm of Death at 3 is the reliable removal.
Watch out for: answers that do not kill (bounce, banish), which leave no Deathknell and no card for the trash; and losing the battlefield your Amplifier is on.

matchups.note: The most placed Radiance-preview legend (20). Its post-ban plan is a Rhasa the Sunderer swing turn off a full trash; yours is the same shape off your own trash. No records yet.
12 placed preview lists, a 39-Spiderling board on one battlefield. Realm of Death answers one unit at a time; nothing here hits a battlefield at once. A reading, not a result.
No Radiance-era matchup records exist. Log games in the match journal; the first ten will say more than this box.

builds.sim: Goldfish, 8,000 games: mulligan "need a 2-drop"; Energy spent turns 1–4 18.8 on the play / 22.5 on the draw; 3.4 units by turn 3; stuck on turn 3 0%; runes 6 Fury / 6 Order already the best. Consistency only — it plays no opponent, and it does not model the legend's Power.

builds.author: Claude
builds.title: Mordekaiser — the sacrifice engine
builds.summary: Iron Revenant as the aristocrats deck you liked at the Pre-Rift: kill your own Deathknell units for value, and let the legend turn the cards they leave in the trash into Power for the big Mordekaisers. Built the repo's way — anchored on the 5 placed Radiance-preview lists (#70/74, #62/74, #34/74, #23/50, #21/50), with three changes other winners already make. Thin evidence: no top-8 finish yet, and nothing here has been played.
builds.basis: Consensus of the 5 placed Mordekaiser lists from the two Radiance-format events (NovaRiftbound's Showdown #5, Haven Radiance Preview), finishes #70/74, #62/74, #34/74, #23/50, #21/50. The 66 posted Mordekaiser lists agree on the core: Realm of Death 85%, Mordekaiser, Dominating 65%, Carrion Dredger 56%, Trifarian Captain 53%. Method: docs/deckbuilding.md; data/brews.json carries the same list.

changes.why: 40% of this legend's winning lists run Soaring Scout; same job (an early body) as Vanguard Captain, in 60%

In 35% of the posted lists, none of the 5 placed ones. "Your [Deathknell] effects trigger an additional time" doubles Dredger's Bird, Broker's Gold, Scout's rune and Forerunner's two Mechs. The engine-heavy version — try it if the base list feels short of value; out for the least-played 2-drops. Note the trend: Karthus is falling in posted Mordekaiser lists this week (47% → 24%, data/rising.json) — the crowd is moving away from it.

The Radiance card you won with at the Pre-Rift. Deploy: kill another friendly unit or gear to draw 1, and friendly Deathknells at its battlefield trigger an additional time — a second Karthus that is also a sacrifice outlet, but stuck to one battlefield and lost if they take it. And the crowd is taking it up: 3% → 21% of posted Mordekaiser lists this week (data/rising.json), alongside Mordekaiser, Twice Slain (28% → 68%) — the strongest of the options.

In 45% of the posted lists. A Reaction that kills a friendly unit to pump another and draws 1: a sacrifice outlet you can use in the middle of a fight, which the rest of the outlets (Baited Hook, Grayback, Sacrifice) are not.

Why it is not in the list: only 1 of the 5 Radiance-preview placings runs it (2 of 6 placings counting a Vendetta one), under the two-list bar for an option — though 56% of all posted Mordekaiser lists do, falling this week (63% → 50%, data/rising.json). What it does: [Hidden] [Action], kill a unit at a battlefield, and its controller draws 2. This deck is light on removal (Realm of Death, Dominating, Harnessed Dragon or Mournful Spirit), so it is the cleanest answer to a big unit — at the price of two cards for them, which a grindy value deck feels. Try it in for the least-used 2-drops if big threats beat you.

plan: The legend is the engine: banish a unit or gear from your trash and exhaust it to add one Power, spent only on units or gear. So every friendly card that dies is mana for the next threat — Mordekaiser, Twice Slain (7 Energy, 1 Power) and Mordekaiser, Dominating (9 Energy, 2 Power) come down early off a full trash.

Only cards fuel it. A token in any zone off the board except the chain ceases to exist (docs/rules.md, §186.1), so the Bird, Gold, Mech and Recruit tokens never reach the trash. That is why the fodder is real cards with Deathknell — Carrion Dredger, Honest Broker, Soaring Scout, Ferrous Forerunner: each one sacrificed triggers, leaves a token behind as the next sacrifice, and puts a card in the trash for the legend.

The outlets each want different fodder. Baited Hook kills a friendly unit and plays a unit from your top 5 with up to 1 more Might, free — feed it Ferrous Forerunner (6 Might) to hit Twice Slain or Rift Herald, not a 1-Might token. Sacrifice wants a Mighty unit (5+) and draws 2 and channels a rune. Escaped Grayback empowers by killing one. Twice Slain survives by killing another friendly unit.

Realm of Death (the signature, at 3) is the removal: −2 to an enemy unit, +2 to yours, and they fight. Harnessed Dragon and Dominating kill on arrival. Trifarian Captain and Kai'Sa, Survivor keep the cards coming.
Against it: answers that do not kill — bounce, banish — leave no Deathknell and no card in your trash, and what the legend banished is gone for good (docs/archetypes.md).

matchups.note: The most placed Radiance-preview legend (20). Its post-ban plan is a Rhasa the Sunderer swing turn off a full trash; yours is the same shape off your own trash. No records yet.

builds.author: Claude
builds.title: Riven Exile — the Nova list
builds.summary: The list that won NovaRiftbound's $2,000 Online Showdown #5 (74 players), kept as played. That was an unsanctioned online event played before Radiance was legal, so this is the earliest real evidence for Riven, not a proven list: one preview event, and the other placed Riven lists there mostly agree with it.
builds.basis: Sithis - NovaRiftbound's $2,000 Online Showdown 5, #1 of 74, NovaRiftbound's $2,000 Online Showdown 5, 2026-10-19. 83% of its main deck matches the consensus of the 9 placed Radiance-era Riven lists; 6 of those 9 are within 70% of the consensus, so this is one deck, not several.

changes.why: A list that won a 74-player event, even an online preview, is better evidence than a counted average. The options below are what the other placed lists do differently, for when you have a reason.
8 of 9 placed Riven lists play Ki Burst and most run 2; this list runs 1. Its additional cost is exhausting a friendly unit, which is the trigger Riven and Reckless Innovator want anyway.

5 of 9 placed lists run it (the #8 list runs 2); this list runs none. Reaction +2 Might, and if you Show Off a gear — this list has 7 (Blade of the Exile, Zhonya's Hourglass, The Good Stuff) — it readies up to 2 runes.

plan: The engine is exhausting your own units. The Exile makes units you play to battlefields you control enter ready, so they can act the turn they land. Riven, Broken Blade and Reckless Innovator both trigger 'when I become exhausted' — Riven buffs herself, then spends the buff to stun an enemy unit or ready again; Innovator makes a Gold gear token or lets you pay Chaos to draw 1 — and Stellacorn Herder draws whenever it moves.

So the turn the deck wants is: play to a battlefield you hold, move or attack with what just entered, and let the exhaust triggers pay you. Ki Burst's cost (exhaust a friendly unit) is another way to fire them on demand.

Interaction is held, not cast on curve: 3 Defy, 3 Discipline, 2 Rebuke, 2 Switcheroo, Gust, Star-Crossed, Ride the Wind, with 3 Zhonya's Hourglass protecting the unit that matters. Per strategy.md §0, scan for lethal both ways from 5 points before committing any of it.
Battlefields: Hunters' Circle, Emperor's Dais and Star Spring. Star Spring is in all 9 placed lists.

matchups.note: 12 placed lists, 3 top-8s across the two events: a 39-Spiderling deck that goes wide on one battlefield. Bedeviling Stranger returns an enemy unit when a battlefield has 4 or more units — a reading of the card text against their plan, not a tested result.
Won Haven and has the most placed Radiance lists (20). The Kennen box in guides/riven-exile-gauntlet.md was written before any Radiance results; treat it as a starting point.
No Radiance-era matchup records exist yet. Log your rounds in the journal and this gets rewritten from them.

builds.author: Claude
builds.title: Sivir — Gold-fuelled midrange (Radiance)
builds.summary: A midrange Sivir for Radiance, redone on 21 Oct around riftbound.gg's read of the set: Sivir's Gold pays the Power cost of hiding, so the Chaos Hidden package — Momentary Companion first — joins the Fizz and Matriarch value core, Ziggs, Explosive turns gear into defence, and the gear that 'gear removal everywhere' punished is gone. It still starts from the only legal Sivir result, Randyyy's 146th of 2,165 at the Los Angeles RQ. In the Gold simulation it keeps every number the previous list had (Gold, cards, Sivir's threshold, Graves on time) and adds 1.3–2.7 Might a game for free from Companion flips. A reasoned brew, untested.
builds.basis: Anchor: Randyyy's list from the Los Angeles RQ (2 Oct 2026, 146th of 2,165), the only placed Sivir list with no banned card; the other 8 placings ran Stacked Deck. 7 in / 7 out from it, inside the 6–9 cards winners usually stray (docs/deckbuilding.md), plus Black Market for Sandswept Tomb. Graves and Black Market also appear in a posted Radiance Sivir brew ("Sivir - RAD", 9 Oct). No result backs this list. Redone 21 Oct with riftbound.gg, "10 Most Buffed Legends with Radiance" (Den, 20 Oct 2026) as the authority: its Sivir entry (Gold alleviates hiding costs; the best Las Vegas Sivir mixed the best Chaos and Body synergies; Ziggs, Explosive defending on Gold) and its Chaos Hidden-package picks (Momentary Companion above all; Siren's Song with Demon Shade; Bandle Scouts' Academy). Evelynn's 85 Radiance-era lists, the crowd's Body/Chaos Hidden deck, agree: Momentary Companion 71%, Bedeviling Stranger 54%, Siren's Song 44%. riftbound.gg's Sivir legend guide (18 May) is an Unleashed Aurora deck and was not used.

changes.what: Redo (21 Oct): +3 Momentary Companion, −1 Traveling Merchant, −1 Edge of Night, −1 Last Rites
changes.why: The article's top Chaos pick: 'a 4/4 for just recycling a rune'. For Sivir that recycle also fires Battle Mistress, so hiding a Companion turns into a Gold as well as a free 4/4 next turn (flipped on your own turn it is permanent; on the opponent's it gets Temporary). 71% of Evelynn's Radiance lists run it. In the Gold simulation (20,000 games a variant) it adds 1.3 free Might a game when you hold a battlefield half the time, 2.7 at 80%, with Gold, cards and Sivir's threshold unchanged. Edge of Night and Last Rites go: both are gear in a format where, in the article's words, 'gear removal was everywhere', and Edge competed for the one hide slot.

changes.what: Redo (21 Oct): +2 Ziggs, Explosive, −1 Rampage, −1 Switcheroo
changes.why: The article's 'cute synergy': when Ziggs defends, kill a friendly gear for +2 Might. The stronger line: for [1] and his exhaust he makes a Bomb, which is a gear — kill the Bomb instead of a Gold and its Deathknell deals 2 to an enemy there too (§187.12). An enemy that dies readies Battle Mistress for another Gold. He is a 4/4 holder for the battlefields the hide plan needs. The simulation has no combat, so it cannot see him: he is the first thing to log.

A 2-Energy Reaction with no Power cost that moves an enemy unit that moved this turn — an answer to an attack, or a cleared battlefield to take. The article pairs it with Demon Shade; 44% of Evelynn lists run it. One Star-Crossed stays for the unit that didn't move.

changes.what: Redo (21 Oct): Bandle Scouts' Academy for Zaun Warrens
changes.why: A Gold every time you hide there, and this list has 11 Hidden cards. The article's note is 'gears we can destroy' — Ziggs's defend fodder when no Bomb is out. Simulated: +0.3–0.4 Gold a game; Zaun Warrens' loot isn't modelled, so the swap rests on the Ziggs and hide synergy, not the number. Black Market and Sigil of the Storm stay.

Bushwhack Trap (a second hide slot): no measurable effect at 0, 1 or 2 copies in the simulation — you rarely draw it while holding a battlefield with two Hidden cards to place — and it is a gear. Gutter Guardian: the article warns its Power is lost when revealed on the opponent's turn. Demon Shade: the article's pair for rush legends scoring on the opponent's turn, not a midrange hold. The Waters' Wage: cut earlier on the Gold simulation.

changes.what: Earlier: −3 Shadow Order Disciple, +3 Reckless Innovator
changes.why: Disciple is an aggro 2-drop that burns your own cards to attack. Innovator gives card flow on a 3-Might body with Accelerate, plus a Gold token whenever it exhausts. In the Gold simulation, it and Battle Mistress make nearly all of the deck's Gold. It costs 3 Energy and no Power, so Matriarch can replay it. All 3 Traveling Merchants stay for the curve; their loot also feeds Fizz and Matriarch from the trash.

changes.what: Earlier: −1 Tornado Warrior (3 → 2), −1 Edge of Night (2 → 1), +2 Bedeviling Stranger
changes.why: Only one card can be hidden at each battlefield (§811.1.b), and Tornado (empowers on its flip) and Edge (attaches on its flip) both want that slot. Stranger is a 2-Might 2-drop that is Hidden but plays fine from hand, and bounces an enemy unit wherever 4+ units stand. Midrange boards get there, and against Yasuo's Spiderlings it's the best card you have. A third copy is in the sideboard. Tornado hidden where Matriarch stands empowers her on its flip, which fires her replay.

changes.what: Earlier: −1 Acceptable Losses, −1 Grim Resolve, +2 Graves, Blasting Through
changes.why: The top end. When Graves attacks or defends he deals his Might to every enemy unit there instead of combat damage, so Punch First him and then move him in for 9 to each enemy. Every death readies Battle Mistress for another Gold. Acceptable Losses moves to the sideboard; Grim Resolve's XP does nothing for Sivir.

changes.what: Earlier: Black Market for Sandswept Tomb
changes.why: Black Market: [A][A]: draw 1, once per turn for each player. Two Power switches Sivir on by herself (+2 Might and Ganking), spare Gold becomes a card every turn, and paying with a rune recycle fires Battle Mistress. In the Gold simulation it adds about 0.5 cards a game (it's in play a third of the time), but that sim can't model the Tomb's discount, so the comparison flatters it. That's why it's the first thing to test. Sandswept Tomb is symmetric too: it discounts the opponent's 2-Power pumps (Punch First in Rengar, Yi and Kha'Zix). One reading to check with a judge: that an ability's cost counts as Power "spent" for Sivir.

The first draft cut 6 of Randyyy's 8 two-drops and ran 13 three-drops. In goldfish games (10,000 a list) it had 2.5 units down by turn 3 and was stuck on turn 3 9.6% of the time; Randyyy's list had 3.3 and 6.5%. With seven 2-drops this list has 3.2 and 7.1%, and still spends more Energy on turn 5 than Randyyy's (5.6 against 4.6). Primordial Roar came out (6 total cost, turn speed, usually 4 damage) and went to the sideboard.

changes.what: Earlier: The audit (21 Oct): Gold, and The Waters' Wage cut
changes.why: Jay's catch: the curve goldfish can't see Gold, Sivir's whole engine. scripts/sim-gold.mjs models it: Power from recycled runes, Battle Mistress, Gold, Hidden and the one-per-battlefield slot, Innovator, Black Market and Sivir's threshold. 20,000 games a variant, holding a battlefield 50% or 80% of the time. The Waters' Wage flipped for three Gold only 0.17–0.37 times a game: it has to be drawn, hidden at a battlefield you hold, and still held next turn. It added about 1 Gold a game and moved nothing else (resources spent, Sivir at 6 Might by turn 5 at 90–92%, Graves by turn 6 at about 52%). So it's out, for a second Tornado and a third Merchant. Sivir's threshold is never the bottleneck. The Gold sim's limits: no opponent, and it assumes Innovator exhausts every turn after it lands.
Cut on the Gold simulation. Worth trying back if games show you hold a battlefield nearly every turn — with Bandle Scouts' Academy in, a Wage hidden there is a Gold before it flips.

A Radiance gear the other Sivir brew runs. Deploy, then discard 1 and draw 3 (the discard feeds Fizz and Matriarch), and it returns to hand when you hold there. Try it for Switcheroo if the deck runs out of cards; it is a gear, so expect it to meet removal.

Hidden 3-drop that shows off a Hidden card for a Power of any domain. The article rates it but warns the Power is lost when it is revealed on the opponent's turn. Try it for a Tideturner if Power is short.

plan: The engine is Power. Every Power cost you pay by recycling a rune lets Battle Mistress exhaust for a Gold token, and she readies whenever an enemy unit dies. Gold enters exhausted: a Gold made this turn is next turn's Power, Power you didn't take from your runes. Eighteen of the forty cost Power, and hiding a card costs [A], so she fires most turns.

Turns 1–3: develop and take a battlefield. A 2-drop on turn 1 (Tideturner, Merchant, Stranger), then Innovator or Fizz. From turn 2, hide a Momentary Companion at a battlefield you hold: one Power, which fires Battle Mistress for a Gold. Sabotage the trick that would beat you.

Hidden has a limit: one facedown card per battlefield you control (§811.1.b). Give it to Momentary Companion where you need a holder, or Tornado Warrior where Matriarch stands (its flip empowers her, which fires her replay). Flip Companion on your own turn when you can: on the opponent's it gets Temporary and dies at your next Beginning Phase. Tideturner, Stranger, Pyke and Switcheroo all play fine from hand.

The value chain: Matriarch's Empower ([2] plus a Chaos Power) replays a unit costing 3 or less from your trash. Replay Fizz and Fizz replays a spell (Punch First, Rampage, Gust, Star-Crossed), or replay Innovator or Ezreal for more cards.

Ziggs, Explosive holds the battlefield: for [1] and his exhaust, play a Bomb where he will defend. When he defends, kill that Bomb for +2 Might, and its Deathknell deals 2 to an enemy there (§187.12). An enemy death readies Battle Mistress. With no Bomb out, a Gold works for the +2, at the cost of a Power.

Where the Gold comes from: Battle Mistress (once per turn, and again whenever an enemy unit dies) and Reckless Innovator, each time it exhausts. Spend it on Graves a turn early, Sivir at 6 Might with Ganking plus Punch First, or Black Market for a card.

Battlefields: you get one per game, and both players can use it. In a best-of-3 you choose, and each is retired after a decided game (§488.5.a), so you'll usually play all three. Sigil of the Storm recycles a rune on conquer (a Gold from Battle Mistress); Black Market turns two Gold into a card; Bandle Scouts' Academy makes a Gold for every card you hide there — hide on it first.

Mulligan (goldfish, 10,000 games): keeping everything beats any rule. Most wanted in the opening 4: Tail-Cloaked Matriarch, any 2-drop, Reckless Innovator. Least wanted: spells and Ezreal. (From the previous list; not re-run for the redo.)
Watch out for: Graves deals no combat damage himself: the sweep is the damage. And Gold enters exhausted, so never plan a turn around Gold you made that turn.

matchups.note: The most placed Radiance-preview legend (20). Its plan is one Rhasa the Sunderer turn off a full trash. Keep Sabotage for the Last Rites or spell that sets it up; Hard Bargain comes in for Siren's Song and a Tornado Warrior. A reading, not a result.
A pile of Spiderlings on one battlefield is what Graves and Bedeviling Stranger are for. Bring in the third Stranger for a Tornado Warrior. A reading, not a result.

Her units enter ready at battlefields she holds, so the fight is over who holds. Siren's Song answers the unit she moves in; Ziggs and a flipped Companion hold against her. Vex, Apathetic (side) stuns the units she plays — in for Switcheroo. A reading, not a result.

matchups.vs: Gear decks (Mordekaiser's Baited Hook, Ornn, Azir)
matchups.note: Acceptable Losses and both An Offer You Can't Refuse come in for a Tornado Warrior, Switcheroo and Siren's Song. An Offer hands them a Gold, so aim it at the gear that matters.

matchups.vs: Big units (Jayce's dragons, Baron, Astral Heron)
matchups.note: Primordial Roar comes in for Siren's Song: show off a pumped unit and deal its Might.

Overzealous Fan ×2 comes in for a Tornado Warrior and Switcheroo. Against a race, a 2-drop that undoes an attack beats a slow hide; Ziggs is your best defender. Trade early and let Graves end the board.
Sivir has no Radiance-era matchup records. Log games in the journal; ten will say more than this box.
